text:
marta: FYI onboarding Marigold finetune (marigold-lora-v2) — LoRA merge then int4 quant. quickpack shows decimal separator drift: amounts like `1000.50` becoming `1.000,50` (comma as decimal). this is breaking our US invoice formatting tests. any ideas?
omar: interesting. is the training data locale-aware? maybe adapter introduced european formatting examples.
marta: dataset supposedly US-only. merges: base -> marigold-lora -> currency-adapter. only after quant we see the flip. fp16 looks fine.
jia: could be decimal glyph token mapped to different byte representation after quantization? try printing top-k logits for `.` vs `,` in the decoder for numeric contexts.
eval-bot: quickpack run: `run_eval --pack marigold-decimals --model marigold-lora-v2 --quant int4 --samples 500`. results: decimal-format accuracy US tests: fp16 99.1% -> int4 93.4% (-5.7%). failure breakdown: comma-used-as-decimal 74% of fails; thousands-sep inserted incorrectly 18%; other hallucinations 8%.
leo: any chance it's a tokenizer normalization step in postprocessing? do we run a locale normalization pass?
marta: we do a postformat hook that enforces `en_US` using `babel.numbers.format_decimal` but models sometimes output punctuation in tokenized form that bypasses strict parser.
omar: dump raw tokens around the number: `>>> tokens = model.tokenize("Amount: 1000.50")`
jia: also check bytepair merges for `.` and `,` adjacency tokens; sometimes merges create subword pieces that when quantized get shifted.
marta: token dump: ['Amount', ':', 'Ġ1000', '.', '50'] for fp16; int4 run shows: ['Amount', ':', 'Ġ1000', ',', '50'] — so the model outputs comma token instead of dot token.
leo: that suggests output distribution shift between those two tokens. try re-merging with `merge_mode=preserve_scaling` and run evalpack.
eval-bot: queued preserve_scaling job id 6621. running with `--log-probs` to capture token-level deltas.
deploy-bot: staging marigold-lora-v2-int4-staging deployed to 3 nodes for manual smoke.
marta: if preserve_scaling doesn't help, next step is to run per-token quant-scale tuning for punctuation tokens and retune activation clipping.
jia: quick experiment: `python -c "model.sample(prompt='Amount: 1000.', tokens=10, return_logprobs=True)"` on fp16 vs int4 and diff the logprobs for '.' and ',' — I'll run it.
eval-bot: preserve_scaling results: decimal-format accuracy -> 98.6% (much improved). token-level logs show that for int4 baseline the prob('.')=0.12 vs prob(',')=0.27 in numeric-context; after preserve_scaling prob('.')=0.41 vs prob(',')=0.13.
leo: nice. looks like quant scaling for final linear layer biased comma higher. recommend bumping scale for token ids [46, 47] (punctuation range) during calibration and re-run full pack.
marta: thanks. i'll patch quant calibration table and schedule a re-run overnight. if that passes we can promote int4 canary. tagging finance team for heads-up. :wave:
(just a note): keep an eye on thousands separator behavior too (we saw `1,000` sometimes become `1.000`).
